The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that were behind their purchases
Why, in plain words: The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being updated when new purchases came in, and the account pages likely showed those copies without checking them against the purchases; what stopped the updates is not known.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 6m 16s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #526 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that were behind their purchases
Incident: CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:04:08 UTC, not back to normal by 02:10:24 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:15:34 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:09:57 UTC
Ended by: Argus: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed, nothing to put back

Summary
The service broke at 02:04:08 UTC and was not back to normal by 02:10:24 UTC, at least 6 minutes 16 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being updated when new purchases came in, and the account pages likely showed those copies without checking them against the purchases; what stopped the updates is not known. What Argus did: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed, nothing to put back. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #526, for a person to review and merge. Nothing was keeping the cached spend figures up to date, so any shopper's figure could go stale again with their next purchase and be shown on their account page.

Impact
at least 6m 16s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 90 of 240 cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind: the widest gap is 88.46, the most any one figure is missing is 1 purchase, and the oldest purchase none of them account for was recorded at 2026-11-10T23:11:00Z, which is when the copies stopped keeping up, and they were being served from 2026-11-11T02:04:08Z. Discarding the entries listed will send those pages back to the purchase ledger, which never moved. The list is what disagreed when this check ran: nothing is putting the copies right, so a figure goes stale as soon as its shopper buys again and a later check will name more.

Root cause and contributing factors
From Nov 10, 23:11 UTC the cached spend totals stopped being updated as new purchases were recorded, so the cached copies fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct, and account pages were served those copies from 02:04:08 UTC. The evidence does not show what stopped the updates.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that did not match the purchases behind them.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 The pages took their spend figures from cached copies that had fallen behind the purchase ledger. The ledger itself was correct and never moved, and only the cached copies were wrong.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T19 02:10:24 Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded 90 of io-shop's stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong
why 2 From Nov 10, 23:11 UTC the cached copies stopped keeping up with new purchases, and nothing was putting them right. The record does not show what stopped the updates, and no change was found that set this off.
  Evidence:
    AL1
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 5 minutes 45 seconds before Nov 11 02:09:53; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes.
      T7
      T8
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:10:16.
      T15
Contributing factors
- Code-Fix read the account page's code in src/io_shop/account_page.py. In that reading, when the cache returns an entry, the page shows that entry's figure without comparing the purchase count stored with it to the shopper's purchases, which the page already has in hand. In the files Code-Fix read, the only check that treats a count mismatch as a sign of a stale entry is an offline reconciliation check, not on the serving path. (AI-2)
- No alert was seen that would catch the cached spend figures no longer being updated. The fault was found only by the check comparing cached figures with the purchases behind them, after the stale copies were already being served. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from Nov 10, 2026, 23:11 UTC and began being served stale at 02:04:08 UTC. The ledger is right and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, config change or rollout is recorded. | 0.75 | confirmed
C2 | The internal cache service io-summary-cache, owned by checkout-platform, is failing to apply updates and so serves stale spend figures. | 0.15 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
C1 was confirmed, but Argus could not tie io-summary-cache to any change it read.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:10:22 | Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1 | Argus | nothing to put back | confirmed
 | 02:12:25 | Proposed a fix: PR #526 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:04:08 UTC. CachedSpendTotalsAreStale fired at 02:09:53 UTC, 5 minutes 45 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #526 | open
AI-3 | Find what stopped the cached spend figures in io-summary-cache from being updated with new purchases from Nov 10, 23:11 UTC, and get those updates running again, working with checkout-platform, which owns io-summary-cache. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add an alert that fires when the cached spend figures stop being updated with new purchases, separate from the check that compares the figures being served. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link the CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert to on-call so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out why the investigation got no metrics and no log lines back for io-shop, and fix it. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert itself listed which cached figures disagreed and when the copies stopped keeping up, which gave the mitigation an exact list of entries to discard.
- 29 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1.
- 31 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded `90` of `io-shop`'s stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong.
- 2 minutes 32 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #526.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was asked to look into why the cached figures had stopped being updated.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 11 02:04:08 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 02:09:53 | DETECTED | CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop fired
T1 | 02:09:53 |  | Argus Received CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
T2 | 02:10:02 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up

T9 | 02:10:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 02:10:14 |  | Investigator Agent Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
T11 | 02:10:14 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 3 hours before Nov 11 02:09:08

T16 | 02:10:20 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
T17 | 02:10:22 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1
T18 | 02:10:23 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T19 | 02:10:24 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded 90 of io-shop's stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong
T20 | 02:12:25 |  | Code-Fix Agent Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #526

Response effort
none - engineer time
166,850 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/f715d8af-c6bd-446a-9d1a-0dbc20ac3283
The fix it proposed: PR #526 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/526) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Read; none came back.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/account_page.py, _the_figure_for asks the cache first. If cached_summary returns an entry, it returns found.amount_cents as the page's figure and does no other check. According to src/io_shop/summary_cache.py, each entry stores two things: the figure, and items_counted, the number of purchases the figure was worked out from. The page already has the shopper's Account and its purchases in hand. But it never compares the two, so once whatever keeps the cache up to date stops, every entry it can read is shown as current. This is the failure the investigation describes: the purchase ledger is correct and the cached copy is behind, so shoppers saw stale figures. src/io_shop/cache_reconciliation.py treats a mismatch in items_counted as a sign of a stale entry, but only in an offline check, never on the serving path.

The fix: _the_figure_for now uses a cached entry only if found.items_counted == len(account.purchases). If the counts differ, it falls through to render_spend_summary, the same path a cache miss already takes. So a stale entry costs one recomputation instead of a wrong figure. Checking the count is just the length of a tuple already in memory, so the cache still saves the walk through the purchase history. Nothing about the cache being unreachable changes. That case is still reported in cache_failure and does not fail the page. With no cache configured, the page behaves as before.

Tests (tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py): the a_cache_holding helper now takes the purchase count the entry claims. The existing "served from cache" test now uses an entry that matches its 2-purchase account; it previously claimed 8 purchases, which is exactly the mismatch this change rejects. A new test gives the page an entry that is one purchase short. It asserts that the page shows the figure worked out from the purchases (2000), not the cached 999, and that served_from_cache is False. Against the current code, that test would get 999 from the cache.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
○ Key incident data collected (for a person)
  no minute of metrics came back for the incident window; collecting them is for a person
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  the chain does not reach a cause
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, some shoppers' account pages showed spending totals that were behind their actual purchases. The incident lasted {duration}. The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's spending total, and those copies stopped being updated when new purchases came in. The account pages likely showed those saved copies without checking them against the purchases. What stopped the updates is not yet known. Argus estimated the cost to the shop's takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, so no one on call had to respond. To end the incident, Argus discarded the outdated saved figures and confirmed this was done. Argus also proposed a fix, which is still a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
